moments.title: Absolute return tells you the gain but not how long it took
moments.summary: The facilitator defines absolute rate of return: 10 lakhs growing to 13 lakhs is a 3 lakh gain shown as a percentage, and the number says nothing about whether it took five years or ten.
moments.evidence: it doesn't matter if the return to 5 years to grow, 10 years to grow none of that it's only giving you an absolute rate of return

moments.title: Same 10 to 13 lakhs in one year or in five — which is better?
moments.summary: The class is asked to compare two investments with identical absolute gains over different periods, and answers the one-year one, making the point that the time you stayed invested matters and absolute return ignores it.
moments.evidence: investment grew from 10 lakhs to 13 lakhs within one year versus if that same another investment to gain from 10 lakhs to 13 lakhs within 5 years which one is a better one?
